figures.claim: 3. Figure 3: Repair success rate by IIS size. Left: absolute counts of repaired instances. Right: repair success rate (%). The dashed red line marks K = 5, the truncation threshold. Repairs concentrate in small-IIS instances (1-2 constraints), with near-zero success in the truncation regime (IIS > 5).
figures.explanation: Execution stage: The qualitative claims in Figure 3's description are supported by partial data: repairs do concentrate in small-IIS instances (4/7 repaired have IIS=1-2), and truncation regime success is near-zero (1/16=6.25%). However, the complete per-IIS-size distribution for all 31 infeasible instances is unavailable (IIS sizes of 9 non-truncated, non-repaired instances are missing), and no plotting script exists to regenerate Figure 3. Without the full data and a plotting script, the exact figure cannot be reproduced or verified against the paper's description.
figures.evidence: From exp/results/summary_table.json: 16 truncation-regime instances (IIS>5) with IIS sizes {61:12, 63:7, 64:9, 66:13, 72:11, 75:7, 81:10, 84:9, 85:11, 86:6, 93:11, 95:7, 97:11, 98:7, 131:33, 134:16}; 15 non-truncated instances (IIS<=5); 31 total infeasible. From effectiveness_evaluation_report.md: 7 repaired instances (72B best) have IIS sizes 1,1,2,2,4,4,6 — 4 of 7 have IIS<=2 (1-2 constraints), 1 of 16 truncation-regime repaired (6.25%). Truncation regime repair rate = 6.25%, non-truncated = 40%.
